title: Run-rate capacity shadow book — Q3 2028 planning
body:
Purpose:
Short working workbook for modeling a conservative
'run-rate shadow book' that ties token-price movements to required capacity (GPU hours), headcount phasing, and expected monthly burn. This is intentionally terse — used for a 30-minute sync with product and infra before the end-of-quarter cadence.

TL;DR (headline numbers):
- Baseline run-rate (current customers + funnel): 1.6B tokens/month (mixed gen/embeddings)
- Baseline marginal cost: $0.0028 / 1k tokens (across hosted + dedicated blending)
- Current committed capacity cover: 85% of baseline; 15% reliant on spot/burst
- Shadow-book buffer target (conservative): 30% capacity reserve for Q3-2028 plan
- Hiring impact to meet +30% buffer: incremental 12 FTEs (infra ops + SRE + field eng ops) phased across 4 months

Assumptions (callouts):
- Token mix: 72% generation (avg response length 140 tokens), 28% embeddings/rerank.
- Model mix shift: assumed 15% of gen traffic migrates to quantized variants in baseline (reduced cost per token by 18%).
- GPU mix: 60% A100-equivalent reserved, 25% spot/V100, 15% on-prem dedicated pools for enterprise customers.
- Spot volatility: assume 20% spot unavailability risk during peak (used to size buffer).
- Price elasticity (customer usage vs price change): short-tail estimate used for sensitivity below (low-fidelity): -0.35 baseline elasticity for high-volume customers, -0.7 for SMB/self-serve.

Sheet A — Baseline weekly cadence (simplified):
Week | Tokens (M) | Marginal cost /1k | Marginal $ | Commited GPU hrs | Spot GPU hrs | HC delta (FTE) | Burn delta ($k)
W1   | 400        | 0.0028            | 1,120      | 1,200            | 220          | 0               | 0
W2   | 380        | 0.0029            | 1,102      | 1,150            | 210          | 0               | 0
W3   | 410        | 0.0027            | 1,107      | 1,220            | 240          | 0               | 0
W4   | 410        | 0.00275           | 1,128      | 1,230            | 245          | 0               | 0
Notes: tokens in M; marginal $ = tokens/1000 * marginal cost. These are input-realizable numbers pulled from cost ledger snapshot (Oct 2026).

Sensitivity experiment (pricing moves + capacity consequences) — single-run scenarios:
Scenario | Price change | Expected net token change | Notes on elastic response | Required capacity delta | Hiring impact
Base     | 0%           | 0%                      | baseline                 | 0%                    | 0 FTE
A        | +7.5%        | -2.6%                   | revenue tilt towards enterprise; self-serve dips modestly | -3% GPU hrs (less burst) | -1 FTE (deferred)
B        | +15%         | -6.2%                   | SMB churn / lower adoption; enterprise stable | -7% GPU hrs | -3 FTE (defer/hire freeze)
C        | -10%         | +9.0%                   | price-led adoption in mid-market; more burst usage | +12% GPU hrs | +6 FTE (ops & SRE)
D (shock)| +25%        | -18.0%                  | structural churn across mid/SMB | -20% GPU hrs | -10 FTE (cost savings)
Notes: elasticity numbers are intentionally conservative and calibrated against observed cohort-level changes in H2-2025. We recommend running a cohort-level model if we want >$1M accuracy.

Headcount plan (phased to support +30% buffer):
Role                     | Target hires | Timing (month) | Rationale
Infra Operations         | 5            | M1-M2         | Manage additional capacity on reserved pools, autoscaling config
SRE / Platform           | 3            | M1-M3         | Oncall capacity, incident mean time reduction for burst windows
Field Engineering Ops    | 2            | M2-M3         | Customer-specific routing and SLAs for dedicated customers
Finance / Billing (contractor) | 2       | M1            | Billing reconciliations for capacity commitments and credits
Total incremental FTE   | 12           | phased        | incremental fully-burdened monthly comp ~$120k per FTE

Projected monthly burn impact (steady-state +30% buffer):
- Additional infra runcost (GPU lease + egress): $210k/mo
- Additional people cost (12 FTE blended): $120k/mo (amortized hires & ramp)
- Total incremental burn: $330k/mo
- Offsets: pricing uplift (scenario dependent) or capacity optimization (caching, batching) estimated to net $60k–$150k/mo if optimization program executed in parallel.

Break-even sensitivity (how much price or adoption shift to cover incremental burn):
- If we keep volume steady, need a blended price increase of ~3.7% to cover $330k/mo incremental at current revenue run-rate (assumes $9M/mo revenue run-rate).
- If optimization reduces marginal cost by 10% (targeted quant+batching work), incremental burn reduces to ~$260k/mo, lowering break-even price move to ~2.8%.

Operational playbook (quick checklist for Q3 runway ops):
- Trigger rules: if spot availability < 65% for 3 consecutive days, flip to conservative routing and enable paid throttles for self-serve.
- Canary capacity: keep 2 days-worth of burst queued capacity reserved for canaries during new model rollouts.
- Billing guardrail: do not allocate enterprise credits > 8% of committed capacity without an approved offset from sales ops.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Do we want to lean into a short-term price increase for self-serve in Jan '28 or absorb via optimization? (impact matrix above)
- Are we comfortable with a 30% buffer vs 20%? SRE prefers 40% during peak windows (costly).
- Confirm financing runway tolerance: CFO has indicated $1.0M/mo flexible burn cushion for product-led growth experiments — confirm before committing hires.

Action items (owners):
- Ethan Li: run cohort-level elasticity model for SMB (due 2026-11-26) — will produce cohort-level price/adoption curves.
- Ruth Alvarez: update reserved vs spot capacity cost curves (include new pricing from cloud partner) — due 2026-11-18.
- Samir Desai: prototype a lower-token quantized pipeline experiment to validate 10% marginal cost reduction hypothesis — due 2026-12-15.
- Maya Patel (me): consolidate final run-rate shadow book and convert to a 13-week rolling pro-forma for exec finance — due 2026-12-01.

Notes to CFO / execs (short):
This 'shadow book' is intentionally conservative: it assumes spot volatility and modest elasticity. If leadership prefers to prioritize growth over margin, we can present a +30% capacity plan with a different financing overlay. Conversely, we can reduce buffer to 15% and avoid most hires, but risk higher incident exposure and slower SLA response.

Appendix (data sources):
- Cost ledger snapshot: infra-costs-oct-2026.csv (internal ledger export)
- Usage telemetry: prod-token-usage-2026-10.csv
- Past experiment: quant-eval-2026-09 (GitHub PR listed above)

Quick comments / notes to self (scratch):
- Consider a small credit pilot (3 customers) to move them to dedicated pools at a lower blended price to reduce burst unpredictability.
- Check legal on enterprise credit terms if we move credits > 12 months.
